en: To arrive at a place; or to begin doing something; or to have the chance to do something.
ex: What time did you get to the office?
你幾點到辦公室的？

en: Having just enough money to live on and nothing extra.
col: from hand to mouth for years
ex: Many families live from hand to mouth.
許多家庭過著勉強餬口的日子。

en: To occupy time or space; or to start a hobby or job; or to pick something up.
ex: The sofa takes up too much space.
這張沙發占了太多空間。

en: To care for a child until it is grown; or to mention a subject for discussion.
ex: She brought up three children by herself.
她獨自養大了三個孩子。

en: Used to say that something seems to be true or likely to happen.
ph: it looks as if it will rain
ex: It looks as if it's going to rain.
看起來要下雨了。

en: To give money in exchange for goods or services; or to be punished for doing something wrong.
ex: Let me pay for the drinks.
讓我來付飲料錢。

en: To reach the same level or position as someone who was ahead.
ex: Run faster and you'll catch up with them.
跑快點，你就能趕上他們。

en: To put something down; or to give up something; or to state a rule formally.
ex: The government laid down new safety rules.
政府制定了新的安全規定。

en: To enter a building illegally by force; or to suddenly begin to do something.
ex: Thieves broke into the shop last night.
小偷昨晚闖入了商店。

en: To find or meet someone or something by chance; or to be understood in a particular way.
ex: I came across this old photo while cleaning.
打掃時我偶然發現了這張舊照片。

en: To stop doing something because it is too difficult; or to stop a habit.
ex: Don't give up; you're almost there.
別放棄，你快要成功了。

en: To make good use of an opportunity; or to unfairly use someone's weakness for your own benefit.
ex: We took advantage of the good weather to go hiking.
我們趁著好天氣去健行。

en: To begin to do something regularly until it becomes a habit.
col: fall into the habit of snacking
fall into the habit of lying
ex: He fell into the habit of staying up late.
他養成了熬夜的習慣。

en: To spread a story or rumor; or (for a ship) to change direction.
ex: Someone put about a rumor that he was leaving.
有人散播他要離職的謠言。

en: To be separate from others; or to be unmatched or without equal.
ex: The old tower stands alone on the hill.
那座古塔孤立於山丘上。

en: To cause something to happen.
ex: The internet has brought about huge changes.
網路帶來了巨大的改變。

en: To wait for a short time; or to continue in a difficult situation; or to hold something tightly.
ex: Hang on, I'll be right back.
等一下，我馬上回來。

en: To start living in a place permanently; or to become quiet and calm.
col: settle down in a new city
ex: The class settled down when the teacher came in.
老師一進來，全班就安靜了下來。

en: To put out a flame by blowing on it; or (of a tire) to burst suddenly.
ex: Make a wish and blow out the candles.
許個願，然後吹熄蠟燭。

en: To tell a secret; or to pretend; or to allow others to know something.
ex: Don't let on that you know about the party.
別讓人知道你已經知道派對的事。

en: To start a machine, light or tap; or to attack someone suddenly; or to excite someone.
ex: Please turn on the air conditioner.
請打開冷氣。

en: To remove something by cutting; or to stop doing something; or to stop an engine suddenly.
ex: She cut the recipe out of the magazine.
她從雜誌上剪下這份食譜。

en: To give knowledge, tradition or objects to the next generation.
ex: This tradition has been passed down for centuries.
這個傳統已傳承了數百年。

en: To begin doing something, especially work.
ex: She started in on her homework right after school.
她一放學就開始寫作業。

en: To deal with or manage something; or to need or want something.
ex: I could do with a cup of tea.
我想來杯茶。

en: To work together and support each other; or to be consistent and make sense.
ex: We must hang together or we will fail.
我們必須團結，否則就會失敗。

en: To receive a letter, call or message from someone.
ex: I haven't heard from him for months.
我已經好幾個月沒有他的消息了。

en: To stop working; or to lose control of your emotions; or to separate something into smaller parts.
ex: Our car broke down on the highway.
我們的車在高速公路上拋錨了。

syn: go to bed early and rise early
en: To go to bed early and get up early.
ex: Farmers usually keep early hours.
農夫通常早睡早起。

en: To be in a position at the back of someone or something; or to give support to someone.
ex: We will stand behind you whatever you decide.
無論你做什麼決定，我們都支持你。

en: To start doing something, especially something that needs to be done.
ex: We need to get going on this project.
我們需要開始進行這個專案了。

en: To watch something happen without taking part in it; or to regard someone or something in a particular way.
ex: The crowd looked on as the firemen fought the blaze.
消防員撲滅大火時，群眾在一旁觀望。

en: To be affected by an illness or a problem.
ex: He suffers from severe back pain.
他飽受嚴重背痛之苦。

en: To mention something casually or accidentally while talking.
ex: She let drop a remark about her new job.
她不經意地提到了她的新工作。

en: To accidentally drop something; or to reveal something secret by mistake.
ex: He let fall a hint about the surprise.
他不經意透露了驚喜的線索。

en: To remember something that happened in the past.
ex: When I think back, I regret nothing.
回想起來，我毫無後悔。

en: To come out or appear; or to move forward.
ex: No one came forth to claim the lost wallet.
沒有人出面認領那個遺失的錢包。

en: To move toward a place; or to help to make something possible or likely.
ex: We made for the nearest shelter when it started to rain.
開始下雨時，我們朝最近的避難處走去。

en: To begin something again from the beginning.
col: start over with a clean slate
ex: I deleted the file and had to start over.
我把檔案刪了，只好重來。

en: To meet or find someone or something by chance; or (of a feeling) to suddenly affect someone.
ex: We came upon a lovely little cafe.
我們偶然發現了一間可愛的小咖啡館。
